# ethereum-optimism/infra Weekly Report (Aug 23 - 29, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on significantly enhancing the observability and reliability of the Optimism infrastructure, particularly within `proxyd`. The introduction of a new passive transaction UX monitor and refined rate-limiting metrics provides deeper insights into network health and user experience. While the team successfully resolved long-standing interoperability "wedges" and made major strides in consolidating the Superchain starter repository ecosystem, new challenges emerged regarding `kona-node` sequencer stability and gaps in SuperchainERC20 developer tooling.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Proxyd Observability & Monitoring
A major theme this week was improving the visibility of `proxyd` operations to better understand rate-limiting behavior and transaction flow.
*   **Enhanced Rate-Limiting Metrics:** Implemented fixed-cardinality frontend rate-limit metrics to provide better signals on how distinct addresses are affected by rejections, moving beyond simple request counts ([#725](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/725)).
*   **Passive Transaction UX Monitor:** Introduced `tx_monitor`, a new feature that observes successfully forwarded `eth_sendRawTransaction` and `eth_sendRawTransactionConditional` hashes. This includes a refinement to start the inclusion clock at the exact point of request receipt to ensure accurate timing data ([#726](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/726), [#727](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/727)).

### Infrastructure Consolidation & Maintenance
The team initiated a comprehensive audit and cleanup of the Superchain ecosystem's repository footprint.
*   **Starter Example Consolidation:** Following a documentation audit, the team developed a strategy to consolidate five `superchain-starter*` repositories into a single primary repo to improve maintainability. The popular `superchainerc20-starter` will remain independent ([#1014](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/1014), [#1015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/1015)).
*   **Archive Sweep:** Four abandoned repositories were cleared for archiving after confirming no live documentation links to them, though organizational permissions remain a final administrative blocker ([#1017](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/1017)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Supernode Interoperability:** The `op-supernode` cross-safe wedge issue was resolved. Investigation determined the root cause was a known oscillation problem related to parent-hash mismatches on specific chains rather than a fundamental cross-safety bug ([#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22325)).
*   **Kona Configuration:** An issue regarding `RollupConfig` leniency in `kona-node` was closed as "not planned," as the ability to ignore unknown keys is a deliberate design choice to maintain compatibility with older configuration files ([#22682](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22682)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Sequencer Stability:** A critical new issue was identified where the `kona-node` sequencer can become stuck in a `forkchoiceUpdated` loop, causing high CPU usage if the engine reorgs its unsafe head during block building ([#22681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22681)).
*   **Developer Tooling Gaps:** The archiving of older repos revealed a missing capability for developers to check token compatibility with SuperchainERC20, leading to the creation of a new tracking issue to restore this functionality ([#1020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/1020)).
*   **P2P Stalling:** Discussions continue on `kona-node` regarding the `NetworkActor` stalling the P2P swarm during remote-signer calls. Developers are currently evaluating overflow policies and latency injection to confirm the fix ([#22646](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22646)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by high-quality internal auditing and strategic planning. The collaboration between contributors on the "Starter Examples" consolidation demonstrates a proactive approach to reducing technical debt and improving the developer experience. Technical discussions around `kona-node` show a rigorous approach to debugging P2P networking issues, with contributors carefully weighing different architectural fixes (such as queue overflow policies) before implementation.
